QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_8

question.text: Under the SAS framework, when an SIA reports on the monetary SROI ratio of a programme, how is the SIA's report best described?

answer.text: A reasonable assurance opinion on the SROI ratio
A limited assurance opinion expressed as a negative-assurance conclusion on the SROI ratio
An audit or examination under prevailing auditing or attestation standards covering the SROI ratio

A report of findings and conclusions, with an explicit statement that it is not an opinion, attestation, certification or other assurance, and with full disclosure of calculations, estimates, assumptions and limitations behind any monetary measure

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook is explicit that the SIA's report should not be construed as an opinion, attestation, certification or other assurance, and that the procedures performed do not constitute an examination or review under prevailing auditing or attestation standards. Where monetary methods such as SROI are used, the SIA must disclose the calculations, estimates, assumptions and limitations behind them. The Trap: Options A and B both miscast the engagement as an assurance opinion. Option C overstates the work as an audit or attestation. The correct framing is a findings-and-conclusions report with inherent-limitation language and full method disclosure. Note: SROI ratios rely on assumption-heavy proxies, so the workbook's requirement to disclose calculations, estimates, assumptions and limitations is central to keeping the report defensible.
